paragraphs: R' Pazi, father of R' Yehudah. In the Yerushalmi, Berakhot ch. 4 halakhah 1, and Taanit ch. 4 halakhah 1, they said: R' Yose met with R' Yudah ben Pazi and said to him, 'Did you hear this matter from your father?' He said to him, 'Father did not say so.' And Hyman reports in Sanhedrin ch. 2 halakhah 3: R' Yudah ben Pazi in the name of R' Pazi in the name of R' Yohanan. And we find in Yalkut Hosea, remez 524, R'

Pazi said: 'Good' means nothing other than Torah. And in Avodah Zarah chapter 3, end of halakhah 1: one of those of the house of Rabbi Pazi — the patriarch’s family wanted a marriage alliance with him, but he was unwilling, saying that he was not worthy of marrying into so exalted a family; but Hyman infers that apparently he did marry into them, as in Horayot, end of ch. 3, they said: those of bar Pazi and those of bar Hoshaya would go in and ask after the welfare of the Nasi every day, and those of bar Hoshaya were always

first. Those of bar Pazi went and married into the Nasi's house, and [he] wanted to enter first; they came before R' Ami. And in the source abbreviated אס״ר, at the supplied locator כ״ד-ד it is brought explicitly concerning R' Yehudah ben Pazi. And Hyman reports in Chullin 47a: Ulla said, 'I was standing before ben Pazi, and they brought a bird before him and he examined it — and the house of the Nasi sent for him, and he rose and went,' etc. And his death we find in the Yerushalmi, Avodah Zarah ch. 3,
end of halakhah 1: that before his death he commanded, 'Clear the courtyard because of impurity, and set a chair's place for Jehoshaphat.'

notes.text: The named Guggenheimer Avodah Zarah3:1 identifies a member of the house of Rabbi Pazi, not simply Pazi, as declining the patriarch’s proposed marriage alliance. Hyman’s identification and subsequent marriage inference remain his. The same named source says clear the house, whereas Hyman’s supplied account says courtyard.

The bibliographical abbreviation אס״ר and locator כ״ד-ד remain unresolved. The house-of-Pazi and house-of-Hoshaya precedence dispute and the later ben-Pazi account are not collapsed into one proved identity.

The whole printed notice is in volume III, p. 1010. The whole consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 4:1 passage contains the question about the father and the negative answer, followed by an Ayin Tav qualification omitted in Hyman’s abridgment. The whole Sanhedrin 2:3 passage reads Yehudah bar Pazi in the name of Yohanan, whereas Hyman reports an additional intermediate Pazi; his chain is retained as his report. The whole Horayot 3:5 passage concerns the houses of bar Pazi and bar Hoshaya, their daily greeting and precedence, and gives a plural wish to enter first beside Hyman’s singular wording. It is not proof that the unnamed family member, the father of Yehudah, and every later ben-Pazi notice are one man. The whole Avodah Zarah 3:1 passage has one of the house of Rabbi Pazi declining the patriarchal family’s proposal, and says clear the house beside Hyman’s courtyard; its extra King of Judah and concluding saying are not inserted into Hyman’s text. Hyman’s APPARENTLY later-marriage inference remains his. The printed אס״ר כ״ד-ד remains unresolved, and Hyman’s EXPLICITLY CONCERNING Yehudah claim is not an invented work identification.
